newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian police arrest slavemaster, another wanted.
newsitem.headline: Russian police arrest slavemaster, another wanted.

text.p: Police in the northern Russian port of Murmansk have arrested a man accused of enslaving construction workers at his villa and keeping them in chains in the cellar, a newspaper said on Thusrday.
One of the victims, Sergei, told the Izvestia daily he had been enslaved after he left an employer who was not paying properly.

On October 27, his employer's friends brought him back, beat him with a rubber-coated metal stick and locked him up in a small room with a metal door, his feet tied up with chains. Soon after that he was joined by two others.
Sergei, a former sailor from Ukraine, said they were forced to work sometimes 24 hours a day, were not fed properly and were not allowed to use the toilet.
After one of the workers escaped the other two were locked up in a cellar less than one metre (three feet) high. Finally, they also managed to escape and went to the police.
In a similar case in eastern Russia, near the Kazakh border, a man was kept as slave at a farm. He also escaped and told police, but the slavemaster fled to Kazakhstan, Izvestia said.

Millions of Russians lost their savings and jobs during the tough market reforms which began in 1991 and are now living below the official subsistance level. Reports of slavery are rare, although prostitution is widespread
